title: The Cerebral Cortex: Four Lobes, Functional Specialization, & Phineas Gage
description: Tour the neocortex: frontal executive networks, parietal spatial processing, temporal audition and memory, occipital vision, and the case of Phineas Gage.

slides.title: The Wrinkled Neocortex & Six Layers 🧠
slides.content:
# The Outer Sheet of Human Intelligence

The **Cerebral Cortex** is a 2 to 4 mm thick outer sheet of gray matter containing over 16 billion neurons. To fit inside the human cranium, it is heavily folded into elevated ridges (**gyri**) and grooved furrows (**sulci**).

* **Neocortex Architecture**: Composed of **six distinct histological layers** (Layers I through VI).
  * **Layer IV**: Dense granular layer that receives primary sensory inputs from the thalamus (thickest in sensory cortices).
  * **Layer V**: Large pyramidal cells (Betz cells) that project long motor axons to the spinal cord and brainstem (thickest in primary motor cortex).

slides.title: The Four Lobes: Functional Map 🗺️
slides.content:
## The Four Cortical Territories

| Lobe | Major Functional Landmarks | Primary Psychological Roles |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Frontal Lobe** | Primary Motor Cortex (Precentral Gyrus), Broca's Area, Prefrontal Cortex (PFC) | Voluntary movement, motor speech production, executive functions, planning, impulse inhibition, personality. |
| **Parietal Lobe** | Primary Somatosensory Cortex (Postcentral Gyrus), Inferior Parietal Lobule | Processing conscious touch, temperature, proprioception, visuospatial navigation, multisensory integration. |
| **Temporal Lobe** | Primary Auditory Cortex (Heschl's Gyrus), Wernicke's Area, Fusiform Gyrus | Auditory perception, speech comprehension, long-term memory retrieval, facial recognition. |
| **Occipital Lobe** | Primary Visual Cortex (V1 / Striate Cortex) along the Calcarine Sulcus | Early visual feature extraction: edge detection, orientation, contrast, and retinotopic mapping. |

quizData.question: Which cortical lobe contains the primary somatosensory cortex located on the postcentral gyrus?
quizData.explanation: The postcentral gyrus of the parietal lobe houses the primary somatosensory cortex, which maps touch sensations across the body.

slides.title: The Prefrontal Cortex & The Tragedy of Phineas Gage 🔨
slides.content:
## The Seat of Executive Control

The anterior portion of the frontal lobe forms the **Prefrontal Cortex (PFC)**, the evolutionary crown of human cognition. It orchestrates working memory, emotional regulation, abstract reasoning, and moral decision-making.

### The Landmark Case of Phineas Gage (1848):
While working on a Vermont railroad, an accidental explosion propelled a 13-pound, 3.5-foot iron tamping rod through Gage's left cheek, piercing his ventromedial prefrontal cortex and exiting through the top of his skull.

* **The Miracle**: Gage walked away conscious and survived with intact speech, memory, and motor strength!
* **The Transformation**: His personality changed irrevocably. Previously dependable, polite, and shrewd, Gage became 'fitful, irreverent, indulging in the grossest profanity,' unable to stick to plans.
* **Scientific Legacy**: Gage's case provided the world's first definitive proof that specific brain regions localize human personality, moral judgment, and executive inhibition!

slides.title: Neuroscience Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
### Broca's vs. Wernicke's Aphasia

* **Broca's Aphasia (Expressive)**: Lesion to left inferior frontal gyrus. Speech is non-fluent, halting, and effortful, but comprehension remains intact ('broken words').
* **Wernicke's Aphasia (Receptive)**: Lesion to left posterior superior temporal gyrus. Speech is fluent and grammatically effortless but devoid of meaning, with severe impairment in language comprehension ('word salad').
